#7401 1 2006-03-12T23:02:49Z Twistkill
Has anyone else played this game? The game Black, made by Criterion, is underated. Every review claims it's too short, the destructible environments have seams so they're not what they were thought to be, and the AI can be blind sometimes.

The AI is sometimes deaf or blind, yes. Sometimes you can creep up on somoene with a silenced weapon and shoot him in the head from behind, and if there's an enemy right next to him, he won't notice AT ALL. HOWEVER, when the action heats up, the AI isn't as dumb... They can sneak up on you and take away 1/4 of your health or more before you'll know what's happened.

Destructible environments do have seams, but most of the time you won't see them or they'll be destroyed before you can get a chance to see them... and they get destroyed quite realisticly.

Explosions are awesome. Explosions from grenades, rpgs, barrels, etc. all look quite nice when you're trying to stay alive in the middle of a huge firefight... it's atmospheric.

My biggest complaint: the enemies all seem to wear amazing body armor! There are 4 types of enemies: standard, (about 5 or 6 hits... and they rarely appear after level 1... ) armored, (about 15 hits on the average) heavily armored (aka shotgunners... about 28 hits or more for them to die!) and there are 2 types of shielded enemies. And they all come in groups of 2-3 or more!

Well, there's a review for ya. Does anyone else play this game, and what are your opinions on it?

#7554 1 2006-03-22T01:21:34Z Twistkill
I searched for a topic about it already, and surprisingly, no one has made a topic about this game. It's a racing game where you get to tune cars with tricked out parts and run away from the cops when necessary.

This game is better than NFS: UG 2 because cops have returned and the graphics have been improved even more, somehow. EA always manages to amaze me with their games, and again they have made another amazing game. Graphics are outstanding on the cars. Even though the PS2 sometimes shows pixelated lines on curved surfaces, they show less on this game, and I can't believe that EA managed these kinds of graphics on the PS2.

The AI is challenging and competent. If you don't get a perfect start off the line or if you hit traffic too much, just restart the race, because that's how good the AI is. They almost never hit traffic unless you "accidentally" hit them into it.

The game is improved also because cops have returned from when they were on Hot Pursuit 2. However, they are actual challenges because the cops in Hot Pursuit 2 always appeared, no matter what, and it was linear in execution. But in Most Wanted, because it adds an open environment like GTA, they appear when you start to drive recklessly, and they can be dodged and taken out unlike the ones in Hot Pursuit 2. There are a certain number of cars that are originally set out for you at each heat level, and when it gets down to 2 cars, they call for reinforcements that arrive in 2 minutes. You get bounty from destroying cop cars and from how long the pursuit goes, and it will fill up faster depending on your heat level. The longer the pursuit level goes, the higher your heat goes. When the bar reaches the top, it resets and goes to the next heat level, and I'm going to explain them to you in detail here:

Level 1: The local fuzz. Not very intelligent and can be destroyed quite easily. Only 5 cars set out for you.

Level 2: Undercover local cops. Slightly smarter and take a little more effort to destroy. Originally 10 cars set out for you. Roadblocks occasionally set.

Level 3: Gets kinda tough. State authorities. Even smarter than the undercover local cops and take slightly longer to destroy. Roadblocks become more frequent, and there are 15 cars set out for you.

Level 4: You don't want to get to this point. Undercover state authorities. They're very smart and take a long time to destroy. Roadblocks are even more frequent, and they become upgraded to spike strips. If you hit one, you're done. A helicopter will chase you as well, so even if you get away from the ground units, the chopper will still be chasing you, so you can't get away that easily. AND, Rhinos will come after you. No, not the rhino tanks in GTA, rhinos are police SUVs that ram you head on, and during a high-speed chase they can get you real good. 20 CARS SET OUT FOR YOU. OMG

Level 5: Don't get me started. Federal authorities, they drive CORVETTES. Very smart and they utilize all techniques mentioned in level 4, but harder. 25 CARS SET OUT FOR YOU. ZOMFG

Level 6: Only available after beating Career mode, these guys are the ultimate cops. UNDERCOVER FEDERAL AUTHORITIES. And they sometimes use Rhinos during the chase, not just as rams. 35 CARS, OMGWTF. They utilize all techniques previously mentioned and the helicopter has more fuel so it can chase you longer... if you manage to get away from these cops you are indeed a master of this game.

There's a little chase meter when you get into a pursuit. As you dodge and evade the cops, the meter will change to "evade", or if you start to drive too slowly, it will go to "busted" and if it stays in busted too long... well you get busted. You get infractions as you dodge the cops, and everytime you get an infraction you get fines against your car. If you get busted, you will get an impound strike marker against your car and you'll have to pay all fines against your car at that point. If you get 3 impound strikes, your car gets impounded and you will never see it again. If you lose sight from the cops long enough, the chase meter will be replaced with a cooldown meter, and it will fill up as you stay out of sight. If you go to certain parts of the map, (hiding spots), your cooldown meter will fill up 2x as fast. When it fills up, you have successfully evaded the pursuit and it will give you a detailed listing of all bounty and infractions recorded. If they find you during cooldown mode, you have to dodge them all over again.

When you have a high heat level, take your car to the one-stop shop and change the look of your car to lower it. Paint changes lower it teh most, so choose a color, buy it, then go back in and change it again to lower your heat level really fast. Another way that is slower but it doens't cost you money is to simply park your car and use another one for a while. As you win races with that car, the heat on the other car will slowly but surely go down.

The down side to the game: stripped down customization. There are significantly less parts, and less categories to edit entirely. Some of them were actually kinda good, like removing custom headlights/tailights, spinning rims, sound systems in the trunk, spinning rims, and side mirrors. I mean really, who wants custom side mirrors? The only good thing they removed was neon. Neon added more color and style to your ride, and when matched to the right color paint, it looked awesome! But there's no neon! >:( And tuning your car has been downgraded as well. It's just a shoddy little menu on the pause screen, there are less categories, and way less detail to it.

This is by far my longest post! I hope you have read my review of the game.

Has anyone else played this game? And if so, what do you like about it?

#7811 1 2006-04-02T05:12:16Z Twistkill
I'm no grammar nazi, but it makes me mad when people make posts that use too many abbreviations or misspellings. Most of you use pretty good grammar, and some of you even use extremely advanced vocabulary and tricky word structure to make your posts sound awesome, which I can't do.

However, a few members use bad grammar because they are eithier lazy, or just don't like using proper punctuations and stuff. (*cough*Ermacrules29*cough* ) The exceptions are people from another country who don't speak english, yet they try their best to type it. They deserve some credit.

The following is a guide to all the punctuations and capitalizations you'll need to know, as well as some tricky apostrophe words. Here we go:

Section 1: Punctuation

1. Periods. Not the thing that women experience every month, the little dots that come at the end of each sentence. ;O EX: The dog jumped over the fence. You use it when the sentence has finished representing its thought.

2. Commas. These are pretty evil. They sometimes have to be used in places that look like they shouldn't have to be used. They represent a break in thought. EX: As the man ran towards the house, it started to rain.

3. Capitalizations. The first word of every sentence is capitalized. ALWAYS. Every proper noun like someone's name, or the name of a specific place, is capitalized as well. EX: The zebra lives in Africa. Africa is a specific continent, so it is capitalized even though it's at the end of the sentence.

4. Question marks. These represent a question that is asked. Most questions start with the 5 W's: Who, What, Where, When, and Why. How is also used at the start of a question, but it doesn't start with W. EX: Who was the last person to use the bathroom?

Added by Atilla: Questions may also be asked by altering the word order. For example, "That is true." is a statement and "Is that true?" is a question. Questions also often begin with "is", "are" ("Are you hurt?"), "do" ("Do you like my shirt?"), "does" ("Does this shirt make me look fat?"), "can" ("Can you read Japanese?"), "could" ("Could you please hold this for me?"), "would" ("Would you still support the Bill if these amendments were added?"), "will" ("Will you please leave me alone?") and "should" ("Should the engine be making that noise?")

A question mark followed by an exclamation mark indicates that a question is rhetorical (ie, that an answer is not expected): Eg. "Are you insane?!"

"have", "had", and "has" are also commonly used to start questions.~

5. Exclamation points. These are used to represent yelling, or sometimes they're used to represent to get the attention of someone, or even both. EX: Look out for that rock!

Section 2: Sentence structure

Commonly misused words/contractions. These are only a couple of the words that sound the same, but are used differently:

1. They're is the contraction of they are. Used to show that a group of people are doing something. Pretty self-explanatory. EX: They're going to the beach tomorrow.

Their shows possession for a group of people. EX: Their baseball went through the window.

There shows the location of something. EX: My Math book is over there.

2. We're is the contraction of we are. It shows a group of people on "your side" doing something. EX: We're swimming in a pool.

Where is asking the location of something. It's one of the 5 Ws. EX: Where is the guy who stole my sandwich?

Wear shows that someone has clothes on. It also means that soemthing has deteriorated. EX: You should wear the green t-shirt and black jeans. The other wear: The ship shows wear. (Okay, bad example. You won't use wear to show deterioration too often, anyways. )

3. Two is the full spelling of the number 2. It is a number, plain and simple. EX: I have two pairs of shoes.

To shows movement. EX: John is going to the dog track tomorrow.

Too shows an excessive amount of something. EX: I had too many slices of pizza.

4. You're is the contraction of you are. It is making a statement about someone. EX: You're stupid.

Your shows possession for someone. EX: Your car was impounded.

I think that's it for the "your" series...

5. It's is the contraction of it is. It's probably the most used contraction ever. EX: It's boring to sit through a lecture.

Its shows possession. It can be tricky to use. EX: Its legs are broken.

Added by mascote_ponto: You use the apostrophe when you are contracting the word "is"
(Example: It's raining)

But you also use it to indicate a possession.
(Example: Metanet's game is geat.)
I used the example of Metanet, but if I used something ending with a s, after the apostrophe that leter wouldn't be repeated.
(Example: Blue Tetris' comic is great.)
See? I used no s after the apostrophe, because it was already before it.~

Added by Atilla: Plural possesives should have the apostrophe after the s. As in, "The Swans' home ground is the SCG." Group nouns, however, should have the apostrophe before the s. So "The flock's breeding ground was nearby" means there is only one flock, while "The flocks' breeding ground was nearby" means there are multiple flocks.

Too can also be used to mean, uh, "also". For example, I could have said that too can mean "also", too.

We're is also often confused with were, because people are slack and leave the apostrophe out.~

Remember, these are only some of the commonly mispelled words/contractions. There are a lot more.

Section 3: Miscellaneous grammar

I know this is the internet and we all like to use shortcuts. However, when you have more shortcuts than full words, that's a problem. At least try to spell the whole word out, okay? This is annoying: "Wil som1 help me please, tis is annoyin k I rly need help cuz my comp is bein slow n shiz" It actually seems shorter to type the whole word out than to use the shortcuts, because you have to find the right letter to replace it with. Besides, how much time do you think it saves? A couple of seconds? Use common sense.

Punctuation, capitalization, and contractions are the 3 main problems when typing anyways. There are a lot of other things to learn about grammar, including, but not limited to: tenses, conjunctions, verbs, adjectives, nouns, and adverbs.

IF ANYONE WANTS TO ADD SOMETHING, POST IT, AND I WILL ADD IT TO MY POST WITH SOME CREDIT. I will post "This section was added by *username*", and then the end of the edit will be marked with a ~ sign.

Thank you for your time. I hope this will help anyone who needs help with grammar.

#161971 2 2006-04-05T01:56:23Z Twistkill
Right-click and save the image to your computer. Then go to the reply window here, at the bottom of the window you'll see a little box that says "Attach Image" Browse for the picture, then click ok, and then hit reply. You're done! You can do this with any file type, but you can only do one at a time.

If you want to upload multiple images, it's slightly longer:

Save image to your computer. Go to http://www.imageshack.us and host the image. When it's done, at the bottom, you'll see a URL code that says "Direct Link to image" Copy the whole URL, then go to the reply window. At the top, you'll see a button that says IMG. Hit that, paste the URL in the box that pops up, hit ok, and then click reply. The image will show up in your post.

Attaching the image is a little faster, but with imageshack you can post several pictures at once, and you don't have that little "Attached Image" text above your picture.

Rambo Match - Whoever gets the Rambo bow gets super Rambo powers, and only then they get points for kills.
Deathmatch - Simplest mode. Run around and kill every person who's not you. Every man for himself.
Teammatch - Same as Deathmatch, except there are teams.

#8459 1 2006-05-03T22:17:40Z Twistkill
This an RTS game. (RTS stands for Real-Time Strategy, for anyone who doesn't know.) You have to colonize an area, build your economy, amass a military force, then wipe out your opponents. The point of most RTS games is to do that: wipe out your opponent. There are alternate ways to win, like force them to surrender, but it's much more satisfying to clear out all their units in a gruesome fashion..

The game is graphically amazing, but my computer lags unless I turn off some of the advanced graphics options like anti-aliasing and the "bloom" effect. Even then, it's still decent. There are 8 civilizations to choose from, they all have unique units, and strategic advantages and disadvantages. The Portugese get a covered wagon every time they reach a new age, (it transforms into a town center). The Dutch's settlers require money instead of food, but they counter this by having a unique building that makes money just by existing. (Just like gas stations)

If you've played the previous Age of Empire games before, the basic concept of the game is the same. However, the game's biggest new feature is the Home City. Because the game is based on imperial civilizations, you are supported by your mother country and you choose upgrades and units that are delivered to your Town Center. The units and upgrades are used in a card system, and you can only choose new cards when you advance in level. Whenever you play in a Skirmish, you gain experience, and that levels up your home city, (like an RPG) which you can use to your advantage to pwn the face of some newb online. Even with an advanced home city, if you can't actually play the game well, you'll be in trouble, because the game is still based on skill.

Another new feature is the ability to build trading posts. Settlers or your explorer can build a trading post. When built along a trade route, you can choose what resource you get every time the trader passes by. The trader strolls on by the trade route, and he delievers whatever resource you select at each trading post. Another new feature: trading posts are also built near Native Settlements. When you build one next to a Native Settlement, you gain them as an ally, and you can train soldiers from their settlement with no increase in your population. There are also lots of different Native settlements, and each one has their own unique units and upgrades to offer. It's almost like a new civilization.

You have three resources to manage: Food, Wood, and "Coin" (Yes, it's actually used like that in the game. ) All three can be used from cards from your Home City, or they can be collected from a trade route. However, the main way to earn them is explained here. You gather food from having settlers hunt wild animals, you can have sheep grow off a livestock pen and then use them for food, or you can also build a Mill, which is slower than the other 2 methods, but it's unlimited and you don't have to go anywhere. Wood can only be gathered from chopping trees. Coin can be dug up from a silver or gold mine. Silver mines start with 2000 coin. Gold mines are hard to come by but they start off with 5000 coin. Coin can also be collected by building a plantation, and having settlers gather coin from it. Like the Mill, it is slower than going into the wild, but it's unlimited, and you don't have to go anywhere. All of these resources are used to purchase military units and upgrades for your civilization.

The game is not a great leap forward in the RTS world, but it is a good step in the right direction. The game is pretty addicting, and it's quite fun to blow the crap out of unsuspecting villagers who just want to harvest their crops. I rate it an 8.7/10

What are your comments/feedback on the game?

EDIT: Fixed some spelling mistakes.

#8546 1 2006-05-07T17:15:29Z Twistkill
I sure post a lot of games in this section. =3

This is an air combat simulator, and it's obviously the 5th in the series. You fly over 25 planes across 28+ missions, with several dificulty levels. Let me start with the graphics. They are excellent when it comes to the planes and mountains, etc. but up-close on the ground they are bleak. But, you hardly notice it when you are flying at over 900 MPH over 20,000 ft in the air. The game has a smooth 60fps, a framerate rarely seen in PS2 games because of the inferior hardware.

There many missions to go through, and a couple of hidden ones. They range from the standard "Shoot down everyone who isn't on your team" to the suppressing fire missions, to the more complex: one mission requires you to escort a weakened plane through an AA gun field by watching the circles on your radar. The circles represent where the AA guns can fire, and you must fly between them. The lower you fly, the smaller the circles are on the radar, which is an advantage. There is also a similiar mission where you must fly through a radar detection area, and circles on your radar represent where they detect planes. Once you navigate through the field, you will come across an airfield where you must take pictures of the planes BEFORE they take off, or else you will have to start all over again. One mission even has fake enemy readings on your HUD.

The gameplay is spectacular, as usual. You can fire regular missiles with a robust lock-on system, (all planes have them) and different planes have different secondary weapons, ranging from bombs to advanced missiles.

There are 4 difficulty levels when you start the game: Beginner, Novice, Medium, and Hard. There are several ranks every time you beat a mission: C, B, A, and S. When you beat EVERY mission with an "S" ranking on normal, you unlock 2 levels even harder than hard mode: Expert and Ace, the hardest difficulty in the game. On Ace difficulty, you can be shot down with one missile!

The planes are all licensed and do exist in real-life, in case you're wondering. <3 The game is noticably speedier than Ace Combat 4, and the ranges for missiles and guns are strangely different: On Ace Combat 4, the farthest range for you to fire a missile was about 800 ft. In Ace Combat 5, it's about 4000 ft. or something like that It's still good.

Has anyone else played any of the Ace Combat games? If so, which was your favorite and why?

#175419 4 2006-05-13T23:22:11Z Twistkill
Episode 5 is the hardest episode in the first column, in my opinion.

I don't know of any tutorials, but I can give you a few tips.

1. The highscores. I don't watch them that often, but they can be helpful sometimes. Don't worry about how fast or amazing the run is, just try to mimic their path at your own speed.

2. Walljumping. I assume you know how to walljump, but you have to time them right so you can be good at the game. Try jumping at them from the edge of a slope to get up the wall fast, or try jumping back and forth between 2 walls, if available. If you just have to traverse on really big wall, you must hold the jump button to get the biggest jump, and then jump as soon as you hit the wall. (Before you start to wallslide)

3. Thwumps. They can be elevators to high areas or transports across dangerous areas if you manage to jump on top of them. When they're moving fast horizontally, you must run with them because they're not considered a solid edge.

4. Gold. Try to get plenty of gold. You might think it's pointless to waste 6 seconds getting 10 pieces of gold, but every piece of gold gives you an extra 2 seconds, so they are helpful in the long run.

5. Don't hesitate. You must be aggressive in jumping and running. 1 wasted second could mean death. Always be alert.

That's some of the advice I could come up with off the top of my head. Hope this helps you.

#175865 40 2006-05-14T19:35:20Z Twistkill
Turn-Ons:

+ Simplicity. When a map is challenging but doesn't have a billion enemies covering the screen, I love it.

+ Challenging without being frustrating. I don't want to pull out my hair and scream at the top of my lungs when I'm trying to beat a map.

+ Big falls with chaingun drones. It looks so cool when N jumps off a ledge and falls halfway down the map while having chainguns shoot at him, and he manages to escape into cave-like tiles for protection. Just make sure it's a necessary fall.

+ Variety. Some chaingun drones mixed with some mine jumping as well as some gold in a tricky spot makes a cool level.

Turn-Offs:

- Insane difficulty. Read my second sentence.

- Unnecessary objects. I want to be able to actually use most of the tiles or objects that are shown.

- Levels that make me go back to the beginning. Especially long levels where it takes me 5 minutes to finish.

- Lag. It makes the level unappealing.

- Linear or symmetrical maps. Some people in this thread have said they like symmetry. I don't really like it, and linear maps (only one way to beat the level) are annoying.

thecalcgenius: Oh, okay. Also, I just remembered that summations are used to show someone's total compensation over any amount of years. You put N (or X) =0, and you put the total amount of years that the person's been working for at the top. Then you put their annual income on the right side + their annual raise times N (or X). There's also a shortcut so you don't have to add up every number individually, but it only works if N (or X) starts at 1, so if you're starting at 0, you plug 0 into the problem to get 0 out of the way, then you put the result on the left side with a + sign. Quote: Atilla, May 27, 2006 10:34 pm
How To Select the Level Data Easily (For Windows):

1. Go to the end of the level entry.
2. Hold ctrl (I assume command does the same for Macs, but don't hold me to it) and press left. This will move the cursor to the last object in the level.
3. Place the cursor in front of the #
4. Hold shift and press home. This will select the entire line before the #.
5. Hold shift and hit right a few times to deselect the name, author etc.

Of course, after 2 you can just use the mouse if you wish.

There's an even easier way. Triple click anywhere on the line and it will select the whole line. Try it yourself.

If you can't find your .sol file, then do this: Right-click the window that N is opened in. Click on settings and go to the folder icon. #189192 2 2006-06-14T04:10:21Z Twistkill
Quote: willow_by_the_well, June 13, 2006 11:41 pm
1) 29-0 crossfire- in replays, I've seen many instances of the ninja bounding up the wall on the left in just two leaps (collecting all the gold) rephrasing my question, how do you gain maximum ascending velocity?
Is there a trick to it. I practically lose all my momentum once I touch the wall

2)in 29-1 hounds

from the replays, the ninja after jumping on the launchpad and rebounding off the small wall next to the pad, reaches the top of the level in a single bound. I am succesful in replicating the move, though very rarely, and can't do it when I needed it. Is there a technique to make it work? How is it explained when you approach the door-switch from the left, you keep the hounds in? Why is it so? Is it a secret? I manage to do it, 1 in ten tries. Is there an explanation?

I can answer your questions.

1. Maximum velocity is attained by not using the launchpad, but by jumping right at the base of the little slope, and jumping again where the slope hits the wall, and it should propel you upwards enough to get all the gold quickly. It is difficult to pull off, so don't worry if you don't get it first try.

2. You must hit the launchpad and jump at virtually the same time. If done correctly, you will be launched upwards with the velocity of the launchpad and the jump from the wall, resulting in a huge jump.

The secret of the exit switch. The door that holds the drones in is concealed behind the exit switch. If you touch the exit switch directly, you will touch the door switch as well, resulting in the drones being released. It is extremely tricky to pull off, but if you just scrape the exit switch, you can activate it without touching the door switch behind it.

I have only pulled off these moves by fluke, so do not get discouraged if you can't get them right away. Good luck.

When you downloaded N, a bunch of files came with it other than N itself. One of them is called userlevels.txt. What you do is Select All and Copy the level data you want from NUMA, then you open your userlevels.txt, and follow the instructions there. Then save your changes and open N again. You'll alos want to make sure that the original copies of N and userlevels.txt are in the same folder they came in. Just create a shortcut on your desktop for easy access.

#193766 2 2006-06-24T04:13:56Z Twistkill
1. The program used to make N is called Flash. It costs a lot of money. Get it here.

2. The source code for any game can be used to modify it to your liking. In this case, N.

3. If you want to clear your progress and you can't find your .sol file, then right-click anywhere in N and click Settings. Click on the Folder icon. Slide the bar all the way to the left and click close. Then close N. Reopen N and your progress should be gone. Make sure to go back to settings and slide the bar back to the right or else it won't save any of your progress again.

I hope this answers your questions.

#199427 2 2006-07-06T01:45:55Z Twistkill
I guess I'll help you.

When you downloaded N, it came with a bunch of .txts in it's folder. One of them is called userlevels.txt. It already has a bunch of them in it, but you can add as many more as you want. To do this, first read the instructions in the userlevels.txt file. Then go to NUMA. On the left-hand side, you will see links. You can click Top-Rated to see the top-rated maps, or Newest to see newer maps that were recently submitted. Then you will see the names of levels, their public rating, (If any) etc. Click on the one you want. You can also go directly any map if you know the URL. When you see the box that says "v1.4+ data", right-click the text inside that box. Select All and Copy it. Then, open up your userlevels.txt file and follow the instructions to complete the process. Open N and go to Userlevels in the Main Menu. It will load the userlevels that are in your userlevels.txt. Select the one you want to play.

One more thing I'd like to tell you: Do not take the N .exe or the userlevels.txt file out of it's original folder that you downloaded. If you want to play N without going through all of your folders, just right-click the N .exe file and make a shortcut on your desktop.

I hope this helps you.

#206681 4 2006-07-24T13:10:28Z Twistkill
It takes more than just saying 'I wanna make DDAs" out of the blue. It will take lots of practice and free time. And maybe a little bit of insanity. Here are some pointers:

1. Try not to use too many launchpads. Especially edited ones. Try to find other methods of propulsion; Thwumps, hidden doors, etc.

2. Not too much gold delay. Gold delay is when you place many pieces of gold on top of each other to stop the ninja from moving when he's on a launchpad, etc.

3. Close calls are a must. Try to make death seem almost impossible to avoid, and then save the ninja at the last second.

Remember, you can't simply jump into making a DDA unless you have patience and the will to learn. These pointers are helpful if you already have the jist for making a DDA. I hope this will help you.

On the topic of viruses, I had an old Gateway computer for a few years. 256 Ram, 2.3 ghz, and a crappy built in graphics controller. My virus protection was not updated, so in the course of those few years I received over 1,000 viruses/spyware onto my hard drive. Eventually, it took about 4 minutes just to get to the log-in screen, and then it took another 15 minutes for the desktop to finish loading. Seriously, no joke. And then when it was finished loading, it ran extremely slow. Programs took about 10 seconds to launch, IE wouldn't even run anymore, (I used Firefox, which is 3x better than IE) and it was generally crappier than my 1992 Mac.

Afterwards, he took it to a repair shop and they said they couldn't reformat the hard drive, it just gave them an error message. That's how f**cked up it was. He bought a new 80 gig hard drive for $75 and the computer ran like new. We sent it to my sister, and I actually got to stay with her the past 2 weeks, so I got to use it. Then, my dad bought himself a Dell Inspiron 6000, (laptop) and a Compaq Presario desktop for me. <3

In short, I had a computer that got really screwed up from viruses, so please don't visit any shady websites or download anything that you don't know is safe. Oh, and update your virus protection constantly.

#215164 3 2006-08-13T19:44:14Z Twistkill
I'm actually gonna write a description unlike pembie...

Boss mode is that the N gameplay area is covered up, so if you are playing this game at work and your boss comes over, you just hit the boss key and it's hidden.

Another advantage of this is that it saves CPU power, so instead of closing N and losing your current process during an episode or making a map, etc. you just hit the boss key.

One last advantage: Whenever a rocket is chasing N or when a laser fires at N in debug mode, if you hit P to go the edit main menu, those noises loop infinitely. Hitting the boss key stops those sounds from looping, and you can keep your progress in whatever you're doing.

So you see, boss mode is quite handy.

#215669 3 2006-08-15T04:15:59Z Twistkill
That's what the debug mode is for, besides editing levels.

1. Copy the level data you want. (If you just want to test a level you've just made, you can skip this) and paste it into the top box in Ned.

2. Then, make sure to click somewhere outside the box and press P.

Make sure caps lock is on, or else you'll be in fbf mode, aka frame-by-frame. You'll have to click the mouse button to advance one frame in fbf mode.

There ya go. Any other problems you need answered, just ask away.

#221750 2 2006-08-30T21:07:08Z Twistkill
Flaming: Basically, calling someone names, arguing, swearing at someone, using derogatory terms, etc.

Trolls are people who flame and annoy other members unpurpose, purely for attention, and feeding a troll is basically adding onto the inflammatory messages, ie. flaming them back, etc.

A PM stands for Personal Message. It is used to send a message to someone that only they can see, instead of asking a random question in the middle of a thread. To send a PM, click the person's username to display their profile. Then, you'll see a button somewhere near the middle to send them a PM. Alternatively, you can just look below the member's posts and click the button.

Hope that helps ya.

#228515 9 2006-09-14T17:12:26Z Twistkill
Quote: GhostfaceN, September 14, 2006 01:00 pm
sorry i have another question. on the options menu there something that say tab button "god mode". i press tab but there is nothing like a god mode or something.
That is not "god mode" as you said, it's called boss mode. Boss mode is that the N gameplay area is covered up, so if you are playing this game at work and your boss comes over, you just hit the boss key and it's hidden. (Or if you're supposed to be doing your homework and your parents come over. )

Another advantage of this is that it saves CPU power, so instead of closing N and losing your current progress during an episode or making a map, etc. you just hit the boss key.

One last advantage: Whenever a rocket is chasing N or when a laser fires at N in debug mode, if you hit P to go the edit main menu, those noises loop infinitely. Hitting the boss key stops those sounds from looping, and you can keep your progress in whatever you're doing.

So you see, boss mode is quite handy.

#230341 3 2006-09-18T20:08:09Z Twistkill
A regular Moderator handles a few sections of the forum. Whichever sections they moderate, they can lock, move, delete, merge/split topics, and they can warn or suspend members.

A Global Moderator handles all sections of the forum. They are not restricted by section.

An Administrator handles all sections of the forum, and they have access to the Admin Control Panel. There they can change almost anything about the forum's looks itself, and not just the members. They can add smilies, change whether or not which sections accumulate posts, change forum titles and/or descriptions, and much more.

Anything else you want to know?

Quote: xdude_rox, September 20, 2006 05:44 pm
I want to start over new, how do I delete my .sol file?
Read this thread for information on where it's located, and then just delete it. When you start up N again, it'll automatically create a blank .sol file.

Alternatively, you can right-click N's window, click on the settings tab, and drag the local storage slider all the way to the left. Close N, reopen it, and your game should be clear. Make sure to go back to the slider and place it all the way to the right again, or else it won't save your progress at all.

#232681 4 2006-09-24T01:07:46Z Twistkill
This is copied straight from the Editor_Manual.txt that comes with N:

1. Press [L] to pull up the textboxes. Paste level data into the upper text box, paste demo data into the lower text box.

2. (Make sure you click outside the boxes when you do this) Press [L] to load your level.

3. Press [3] to load your demo.

4. Press [Q] to initiate playback of the demo.

5. Press [P] to start viewing the demo.

6. Make sure caps lock is on!

There ya go. Reply if you have any further problems.

#1 Isn't a very good response, you know. Although you were trying to help him, I believe you're doing it the wrong way.

To save levels in Ned, Pate_Rake, get the data in Ned from the lower box. It's shown how to get the data in the Ned menu, it's really self-explanatory. Select all and copy the data. Then, open Notepad, (I'm only assuming you're running Windows) and paste the data there, and then save the file. When you want to load the data again, simply select all and copy the data in the file, then open ned, and paste it into the lower box. Press L to load the data, and you have your level ready for editing/playtesting. Make sure you click outside of the box before loading the data with L, or else you will get a NaN, which is a glitch in N level code.

Okay, when you get to the last episode in a column, (Episodes 0-9 is a column, 20-29 is a column, etc.) you only have to reach the last level of that episode to unlock the flavor for beating that column. 5. Press [P] to start viewing the demo.

6. Make sure caps lock is on!

#249820 4 2006-11-04T04:49:59Z Twistkill
Lucky I was playing Soldat just as this thread was made, Ngaged... You helped out with NUMA itself, now lemme give him advice on map-making.

Don't go too overboard submitting as many maps as you possibly can. (Aka "ZOMG LOOK I MAID 13 MAPZ IN 1 DAI!111!1zero!1one") Testing them out, making sure they feel smooth, making sure there aren't too many unnecessary objects, not too much gold or overabundance of mines, etc. is called playtesting. Many new or ignorant (And I use that term lightly) map-makers do not playtest their maps, which results in sloppiness. In short, make sure the map feels right before you submit it.

And... if you do submit more than 2 maps in one day, they will not appear on the newest page right away. They will appear after your other 2 maps have been bumped off the newest page. This is called the queuing system, and it is needed to prevent too many of any one person's maps from flooding the newest page.

Just a heads-up.

#254867 2 2006-11-15T03:14:50Z Twistkill
Perhaps this is the solution:

Right-click anywhere in the window that N is running in, and click on Settings. Then click on the tab that has a folder on it. The slider that is there is for Local Storage, which is how the Flash Player saves data. Make sure the slider is all the way to the right, which is an unlimited amount of storage, and then click Close. I'm pretty sure that is the solution to your problem, but if this persists, you should also try re-downloading N.

If the slider is already currently all the way to the right, I don't know what else could be wrong. You could also try System Restore if you're using Windows XP.

#258333 2 2006-11-23T01:00:40Z Twistkill
Okay then.

Right-click the image you want to post and save it to your computer somewhere. Go here[/b] and upload the image. When you upload it, it will give you some codes. Go to the very bottom one that says "Direct Link to Image", then select all and copy it. Open your reply window, and type this:

[img][/img]

Then paste the URL you copied in between those tags, hit add reply, and you're done.

An alternate method that is somewhat faster, but only allows you to upload one thing at a time, is attaching an image directly to your post. Save the image you want by repeating the first step above, then open the add reply window. Underneath the text area is a bar that allows you to upload anything. Find the picture and then click open. The file path appears. Then hit add reply and you're done.

#259703 5 2006-11-25T23:34:16Z Twistkill
The game is great in its own right. Below is an in-depth, but not completely thorough, overview of the game.

+ indicates a good change. - indicates a bad change. = indicates it could go either way.

= Crew. The crew feature is a unique change. It's not very complex or particularly exciting, but it can make the game a little easier in certain races. There are 3 types of crew members you can hire:

(Crew continued) A blocker can temporarily slow down opponents who are catching up to you. Drawback: They can sometimes mess up and miss your opponents.

(Crew continued) Drafters speed ahead of you, and if you follow behind them for a few seconds, you get a boost of speed when you pass them. Drawback: There aren't too many long straightaways necessary for a good draft.

(Crew continued) Scouts find all the shortcuts possible in a race, and they know the best lines through corners. Drawback: Er... I've honestly never used a Scout before. Sorry. I'll get back to you on this one...

(Crew continued) You can only have 3 crew members available, and you only take one of them with you into races.

- There is no more reason to have the cops chase you anymore. There is no bounty or milestones to achieve, and the cop chases aren't really as exciting.

+ Canyon races. Look in the Boss and Canyon races section for details.

+ Urbanization. The city theme makes a welcome return. It is night-time when you play once more, and overall it has a better feel to it.

- The tier system. The tier system for cars isn't very good, in my opinion. There are 3 tiers, and each tier is better than the last one. You start with Tier 1 cars. When you upgrade it to the max, it's still only better than average. Tier 2s are great when upgraded to the maximum, and Tier 3 can be upgraded the best, but the problem is that it is awkward. I wish there could just be cars like in Most Wanted, they're all great when performance is upgraded to the max... all you would need is the cash. Unfortunately, this is not so.

+ Classes. The class system for cars is a welcome addition. There are 3 classes of cars, and the 3 tiers go along with them, as well: Muscles, Tuners, and Exotics.

(Classes continued) Muscles have the best acceleration in the game, as well as a hefty top speed. They are the best in the straightaways. Their main problem is cornering. You need to slide into corners early to be able to make them correctly, but if handled properly, a Tier 3 muscle can be the best car in the game. (The best is the Chevrolet Corvette)

(Classes continued) Tuners are all about handling. They make tighter turns than the other 2 classes, and their acceleration is pretty good, but their top speed is a little slow. So, don't slow down too much when you're entering a corner and leave your opponents in the wall. The best Tuner... I believe is either the Lancer Evolution 9 or the Nissan Skyline.

(Classes continued) Exotics are kinda mixed. They share a little of the turning ability of the Tuners, yet they share some of the Muscles' speed. They do, however, take skill to drive. If you can outrun your opponents in the corners, and you can find a good line down a straightaway, you can beat almost anyone. I believe the best is the Lamborghini Murcielago.

(Classes continued) So you see, all cars from the 3 classes handle and drive differently, and this is a welcome addition to the game.

= Customization. The Aftermarket system is basically unchanged form Most Wanted, (NFSU 2 had the best customization I've ever seen) but the unique Autosculpt system is kinda neat. Only special parts are used with the system. You actually shape the bumpers, hoods, wheels, etc. that you want. Unfortunately, there aren't enough options for bumpers. Body Kits in the Aftermarket system are still my choice. It all depends on what you prefer.

+ Territories. This is a cool change, and although it's not very in-depth, it works. There are 4 territories in the game, with several zones in each territory, and there are 3 or so races in each zone. When you beat 2 out of 3 races in a particular zone, you gain control of that zone. If you gain control over all of the zones in a territory, you come to the boss race for that territory, (Explained next) and only if you beat the boss will you claim ownership of that territory.

Mostly + Boss and Canyon races. There are only 4 boss races in the game. But, they are more exciting. When you beat all of the zones in a territory, you face the boss. The first race against the boss is a 1-on-1 in the city. Beat him there, and you go the Canyon race. There are 3 canyons, and which one you race in depends on the territory you're trying to take over. It's all downhill.

(Boss and Canyon races continued) In the first race against the boss, you have to stay close to him/her as he/she races down the canyon. A meter displays how close you are to the boss. The closer you are at any particular point, the more points you accumulate. If you start to fall behind, your point accumulation slows down.

(Boss and Canyon races continued) In the second Canyon race, it is the opposite. You are in front and you must try to keep as far ahead of the boss as possible. Whatever points you accumulated in the previous race are what you start with. The farther ahead you are at any particular point, the slower your points decrease, and likewise, if he is sticking on your ass, you lose points faster.

(Boss and Canyon races continued) If, in the first race, you somehow manage to pass the boss for 10 seconds, you automatically win both races. However, if the boss passes you in the second race for 10 seconds, you automatically lose.

(Boss and Canyon races continued) Some of the turns are on the edge of the canyon! If you make these turns too wide, you may hit the edge of the turn and fall of the cliff! You must restart the race from the first Canyon race if this happens.

+ Graphics are even better than Most Wanted, even for the PS2. The cutscenes are amazing. (If that is somehow possible. Damn EA and their haxoring abiliteez)

Phew... This is not a throughly exhaustive overview of the game, but it is quite detailed in its own right. Overall, this game is quite fun, and it is very challenging when you get to the last boss race. The racing action is still clean and exciting, there are several changes to the gameplay, and the graphics are slightly improved.

I think the difficulty for your map would be chosen during the "confirm" step, and only if you selected a "playable" map category. If you're submitting N-art, DDA, test map, or something of that nature; then you wouldn't have the option for the map difficulty.

Anyway, here's my idea of what the difficulties would be:

Code green[/color]: Simple and fun. Not even a challenge, whatsoever, to any experienced player. Heck, even beginners wouldn't have any trouble beating it. This map would be like one you'd find in the first column on N.
Code yellow[/color]: Moderate difficulty. A bit of a challenge. Experts might beat it first try. Novices would require quite a few replays. The gold may present an optional challenge for skilled players. This map would be like one you'd find in one of the middle columns on N, like the 40's or 50's.
Code red[/color]: High difficulty. Even the experts would need a few gos at this map to get it right. Novices need not apply. All-golding the map would be an unrivaled feat of heroism. MTI would be a high-end code red map, as well as a few of the maps in the 80's and 90's column.
Code black[/color]: Nearly impossible--or just straight-up impossible. The best of the best are made fools of by this map. If you consider yourself an "expert", you simply aren't good enough. This map is one which the map-maker is relatively sure to be unbeatable. The mapper does not expect a satisfactory demo. That's not to say the map can't be beaten--however, to beat it, one would need to be of godlike prowess. No map in the game is of this caliber, but a few on NUMA are.

Good system, but the difficulty between Green and Orange is a little too much of a step, don't ya think?

The American High School year system

9th Grade (Freshman): Typically 15 years old by the end of this year.

11th Grade (Junior): Typically 17 years old "
12th Grade (Senior): Typically 18 years old "

#266753 2 2006-12-08T23:59:25Z Twistkill
First and foremost, welcome. By the way, it's just called N. Not N-game.

Boss mode is actually quite useful:

1. Whenever you're playtesting a map in Ned, and the rocket, laser, or N sliding down a slope sound effects starts, if you go back to the main menu, the sounds loop infinitely. Activating Boss mode stops the looping sounds.

2. N, by default, takes up lots of CPU power. Activating boss mode cuts down the amount of CPU power required to run N, so you can go off to do other things and still not lose your progress.

3. The reason why it's called Boss mode: (If you work with computers) Whenever your boss comes by, you can quickly hit the Boss mode button to show that blank screen so he won't suspect much. Also useful if you're slacking off when you're supposed to be doing your homework and your parents stroll by.

So, there ya go.

It's also required that you read the FAQs and the Forum Rules. They tell you the general guidelines and requirements to become a contributing member here, as well as some useful information you should become familiar with.

Have a nice stay. If you have any further problems, you can refer to my signature.

#275216 185 2006-12-22T20:46:56Z Twistkill
I was reading the review of this game on Fun-Motion, and I saw a link to an article about StarForce protection. Clicky. Apparently it may ruin your CD/DVD drivers to the point of unusability, and it's automatically installed with Trackmania Nations. Should I continue with the download of this game?

EDIT: However, here's a quote of a user review on Fun-Motion regarding Starforce:

Quote
#
Dave said,

on September 27th, 2006 at 11:36 pm

In reply to zM (I know the post is old but I hope it will help):

I have read that StarForce drivers have been confirmed as causing reduced optical drive performance (due to Windows stepping down the IDE speed, as the boingboing article describes) although the theory that it actually damages optical drives is probably urban myth IMO (not that I can say authoritatively, of course). The thing to realise is that there are a lot of different versions of StarForce and some work in different ways and may or may not be problematic - its a bit of a lucky dip and you take your chances by installing the software, but most people I should think do not encounter any real problem with it. The good news is that the protection developers provide an uninstall tool (though not on their own website hm) that will thoroughly clean the protection software off your PC if you ever require it:

http://www.onlinesecurity-on.com/protect.phtml?c=55

Having said what I have - that I think that most people will not encounter a problem - I will disclose that if I speak from personal experience then I am not a part of that group. About 2 months back I was finding that my PCs DVD-ROM drive seemed to have difficulty reading discs - it seemed to come about suddenly but it had probably been getting gradually slower over time, and it continued to get worse to the point that it was unusable. Additionally I was also encountering spontaneous crashes and reboots that sometimes happened when I tried to access my drive, or even just loaded a disc into it. In the course of troubleshooting I tried uninstalling and reinstalling the DVD-ROM drivers in Windows a few times, but it didnt seem to help on its own and I next thought of StarForce. I had two games (V8 Supercars 2 and Sudeki) installed that used the protection software so I uninstalled them and ran the sfdrvrem.exe tool; after uninstalling and reinstalling my DVD-ROM drivers a few times more, the disc drive was working properly once again and the system had recovered its stability.

On the evidence of that experience the StarForce drivers look pretty suspect to me, however the fact that tools are provided and were successful in undoing the damage helps redeem it somewhat. Draw what conslusions you will.

#280406 3 2007-01-03T00:56:25Z Twistkill
We appreciate it when people asking for help are coherent and tell us what their problem is clearly.

You must not drag the N.exe or the userlevels.txt out of the original folder it came in, and if you do, you have to make sure both of them are in the same directory, like the desktop, or another folder. If you want easy access to them, you can simply right-click and create a shortcut to the desktop for them, which what I have done.

If that fixes your problem, than read no further. If not:

At the top of your userlevels.txt file, underneath that line that is like this: ***DO NOT MODIFY THIS LINE***, if you do not have "&userdata=" just underneath that, than nothing will show up. Make sure that's there.

If this fixes your problem, then you're good to go.

By the way, welcome to our community. It is required that you read the Forum Rules and the FAQs. It is also recommended that you check out the N Wiki.

Have a nice stay.

(I know George beat me here, because when I opened the Forum index in another Firefox tab to get the above links, I saw his name as the most recent post here.)

#282675 3 2007-01-07T23:12:44Z Twistkill
This is a technique that becomes almost second nature with practice.

First, you must land on a bounceblock with a good amount of momentum. Too slow, you won't get the necessary height, but if your approach is too fast, you will either die on impact or you will survive but you will go through the bounceblock.

When you hit the bounceblock, wait until you're as far down as the block will stretch. When it starts to rise up again, jump up as hard as you can when it's at its peak. This will launch you high up.

There is also another variation of this that involves jumping multiple times. Get your necessary momentum onto the bounceblock, and when it reaches as far down as it will go, jump up twice the moment it starts to rise up again instead of at it's peak. If done correctly, you will get 2 little jumps up to get a huge boost. This can also be done up to 3 jumps if you can hit the jump button quickly enough.

There is a bunch of training levels with descriptions in a topic made by Atilla called St. Atilla's College for Ninja. This trick is described there, as well as many more advanced tricks necessary to become a good N player.

I hope I've been helpful to you.

#284949 2 2007-01-12T23:06:21Z Twistkill
You press Tab to go into Boss mode by default, but you can re-map your keys in the Customize menu.

Boss mode is a feature of N that has several handy features.

1. N itself takes up lots of your processor power, and Boss mode makes N only use a fraction of your processor power so you can do other stuff, like other games, documents, internet porn, etc.

2. Well, it's called Boss mode for a reason! When your boss, parents, dominatrix, etc. comes by, you can simply press the button to hide the N window from view for a minute.

3. An annoying bug in Ned is when you press ~ to go back to the main menu, if a rocket is flying by, N is sliding down a slope, when a laser drone goes by, or when N is smokin some weed, the sounds will loop infinitely. Boss mode stops all of the sounds.

So you see, it's actually quite handy.

#285375 13 2007-01-14T01:03:09Z Twistkill
Quote: cheezos123, January 13, 2007 07:47 pm
man i dont know how to sumbit a map to numa plz someone tell me HOW!!!!!!PPPPPPPPPPPPLLLLLLLLLLEEEEEEEEAAAAAAAASSSSSSSSSEEEEEEEE!!AAGGGGGGHHHHHHH
The need to submit a map to NUMA is not so frustrating that you should react like this. You should also use less smileys, as they can become annoying.

If you do not have a NUMA account, read this part. If you already do, (I'm assuming you don't) then skip ahead to after the ~.

Open N, go into the Customize menu. In the lower right hand corner, enter the required information into those fields, and then click Create New User. Go to your e-mail inbox and check for an activation e-mail. After you've done that, go onto NUMA, and log in on the left-hand side.

~

After that's done, select all and copy the level data generated by Ned. Click on Submit a Map on the left-hand side, and fill in the required fields. When you paste the level into the "Map Data" field, make sure it is just the raw data and not the $Name of map#Author#Type#Data# format. NUMA automatically creates that for you.

For more help regarding N and NUMA, as well as miscellaneous N-related stuff, refer to these links:

N Wiki
FAQs
the editor_manual and readme .txt files that come with your N download.

You should also read the Forum Rules. They lay out the guidelines you should follow to become a respectable member of the community.

Enjoy your stay here.

#294563 4 2007-02-07T01:29:38Z Twistkill
Quote: Oleary15, February 06, 2007 08:08 pm
and how do you make demos? that will be pretty cool if you could do that.
Hello there, Oleary15! We welcome you to the Metanet Forums.

Making demos are indeed possible! The demo recording and playback features of N are explained in the editor_manual.txt that comes with your N download. Here's the section that refers to the demo recording and playback:

Quote: editor_manual.txt
Section 7 Playing and Recording Demos


---Recording a Demo---


1. Create or load a level:  Press [L] to bring up the data textboxes, and paste your level into the top textbox.

2. Press [L] to load the level.

3. Press [1] to start recording the demo.

4. Press [P] to start playing the level, so your exploits can be recorded.

5. Make sure caps lock is on!

6. When youre finished playing and want to stop the demo, press [~] to return to the debug menu.

7. Press [2] to stop recording.

8. Press [4] to save your demo data to the clipboard.

9. Paste demo data to a text file.





---Playing Back a Recorded Demo ---



Note!!  Always paste demo data into the lower text box!

The top textbox should be filled with level data corresponding to the demo -- the level in which the demo should be played.


1. Press [L] to pull up the textboxes.  Paste level data into the upper text box, paste demo data into the lower text box.

2. Press [L] to load your level.

3. Press [3] to load your demo.

4. Press [Q] to initiate playback of the demo.

5. Press [P] to start viewing the demo.

6. Make sure caps lock is on!

In addition, here's all the miscellaneous information you'll need regarding N, Metanet, Robotology, and NUMA:

N Wiki - Very helpful, you should check this out when you're stuck.
Frequently Asked Questions - You should really read these, man. They can be quite helpful.

Also, you need to reference the Forum Rules! We don't want you to end up getting susupended, now, do we?

Have a nice day. If you have any further questions, you refer to my signature.

#296221 11 2007-02-11T15:32:11Z Twistkill
Quote: Alexthegolem, February 11, 2007 09:37 am
Its been off all the time.

What do you mean about resseting my progress? i havent found any button to do that....

The very first post in this thread has the 3 main ways to reset your progress. Deleting your .sol is one of them, which is what you have done.

Go the highscores. Select the episode(s) you cheated on, and look in the upper left hand corner. Do you have a personal best for all the levels in the episode(s)? If you do, then the levels shouldn't come up as cheated; try beating them again. If you don't, then that's the most likely reason for the levels showing up cheated. You must beat all the levels in that episode, from beginning to end, seeing as there is no way to start halfway through an episode.

Try the above solution and see if it works.

It isn't very hard at all.

Copy the data from the map you want on NUMA. The data is labeled 1.4+ data.) Now, go into your userlevels.txt. You see that line that says *****PASTE ALL DATA BELOW THIS LINE*****? Well, that's what you do; You paste the data anywhere underneath that line, (and also underneath the "&userdata=") but make sure it does not interfere with any of the other data you see there. You need to make sure they are all separated from each other.

Now, go to Userlevels in N. Look around for the map you just copied. If you found it, congratulations! If no maps show up at all, then this has happened: You have moved the N.exe (The game itself) out of it's original folder. The userlevels.txt and N must be in the same directory. If you want them easily accessible, make shortcuts to them onto your desktop, but do not drag the original copies out of that folder.

#300378 2 2007-02-23T22:15:44Z Twistkill
Indeed it is possible. There was a thread asking this same question not too long ago, to which I answered. Here's exactly what I wrote there:

It isn't very hard at all.

Copy the data from the map you want from NUMA. (The data is labeled 1.4+ data.) If you want to get whatever saved levels you have from your computer, just add this paramater to the map: "$Name of map#Author of map#Category of map#*paste the data here*#". And make sure the # is at the end of the data. Now, go into your userlevels.txt. You see that line that says *****PASTE ALL DATA BELOW THIS LINE*****? Well, that's what you do; You paste the data anywhere underneath that line, (and also underneath the "&userdata=") but make sure it does not interfere with any of the other data you see there. You need to make sure they are all separated from each other.

Now, go to Userlevels in N. Look around for the map you just copied. If you found it, congratulations! If no maps show up at all, then this has happened: You have moved the N.exe (The game itself) out of it's original folder. The userlevels.txt and N must be in the same directory. If you want them easily accessible, make shortcuts to them onto your desktop, but do not drag the original copies out of that folder.

Now I hope your predicament is solved. If not, reply back with any more inquires you may have. In the future, however, you should really check out the following links for any further questions you have about N, NUMA, Metanet, or this forum.

The N Wiki - Tons of useful information. Definitely worth a look.

The Frequently Asked Questions Read-Only Sub-Forum - Lots of juicy information here. Find useful facts about Robotology, N, and much more!

The Forum Rules - You will need to follow these guidelines. We don't want you to end up getting suspended, now.

Okay, when you enter the room, look near the back. You'll see 2 statues with a glowing-type thing next to them. This (hopefully obviously, by now) means that you can move them around. Move each of them in front of the 2 spawning points of the Harpies, and voila! But wait! For a huge bunch of red orbs: Use Medusa's Gaze on the Harpies while they're flying around, before you plug the spawn points. Whenever you freeze one, it will fall to the ground and break, giving you a 30 orb bonus for breaking the Harpy using Medusa's Gaze. Repeat this many, many times until the game will not allow you to take anymore. There is a health and magic alternating chest behind each statue, so you can continue this for a while. When the game puts a cap on your orbs, or when you've run out of magic, plug up the spawn points.

I can only partially understand what you are inquiring. From what I gather, you have finished making a map in Ned, and you're looking for it to give you the data in this format: "$Map name#Author of map#Category of map#all the data here#" Well, that is the userlevels format, and reading your userlevels.txt should tell you what that is all about. To test out your map in Ned, you should read the editor_manual.txt that comes with your N Download. Here's the section regarding your problem:

Quote
---Saving and Loading Level Data---

After youre finished creating a level, press [home] to return to the edit menu, and then [PGDN] to pull up the level data text boxes, which will then contain your level data.

Click in the top text box and press [CTRL]+[A] (or [Command] + [A] in Mac) to select all the text and [CTRL]+C ([Command] + [C]) to copy it so you can paste it to a text file and save it. 

You can paste level data into the top text box and press [PGUP] to load it into the editor.




We recommend that you document levels like this as you make them:
   
from Bills_levels.txt

//type - action

//space battle 2 demo

------------------

Bill Pullman
25 April 2004
billpullman at whatever dot com



Level names should be short (say, no more than 50 characters), and as descriptive as you can manage.




---Testing Newly Made Levels---

When youre done saving your level, press [~] or [|] from the editor menu to return to the debug menu, where you can play your new level by pressing [P].  See Section 6 for more info on playing in debug mode.

Its important to test each level, to make sure its beatable.  Recording a demo of you beating the level is also a good idea, because then people will believe you when you claim your level's not impossible.


After testing, you can consider your level finished, and try it in User Levels mode, in which you can play it in
game mode rather than debug mode.  Read the included userlevels.txt file for more information on how to add levels.


----------------------------------------Section 5 About Level Data
***skipped this section, but you should read the whole manual regardless.***

----------------------------------------Section 6 Playing in Debug Mode

At the debug menu, you can press [P] to test a level by playing through it.  There are several controls available in debug mode which are added to help debugging and testing.


Gameplay commands

[caps lock] pause / unpause the game
      -turn caps lock on to begin playing, after pressing [P].

[enter] - toggle between alive and dead
-if dead, you will respawn alive at the mouse cursors position. This is useful if you die while testing a level, and want to continue playing it without restarting.
-if alive, you will be killed by a blow in the same direction as the cursor-to-player direction.

[shift] - while dead, hold shift and move the mouse to shove the rag doll around.

[ctrl]/[command] - while dead, hold ctrl/command and move the mouse to drag the rag doll around.

[spacebar] while dead, toggles between exploded and non-exploded.


Note: When the ninja dies in debug mode, objects will continue to behave as if the ninja was alive.

So you see, these instructions are helpful and informative. If you any further questions, you cna read up on the N Wiki or check out the FAQs. You will also need to read the Forum Rules, as they can help you avoid being suspended.

#306106 8 2007-03-18T16:31:08Z Twistkill
Ah, a common inquiry. An easily solved one, at that.

At the top of this forum, click the big black button that says NUMA. Search around for maps that you like. When you found one, copy all the data that says "1.4+ Map data" and go into your userlevels.txt. Read the first part of it. There is a big line that says "***PASTE EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE***", so it's obvious what you do. You paste the data you copied below that line, but make sure it does not interfere with any other level data you currently have, (Make some room between other data) and make sure it is also underneath the &userdata= line.

Now, go into the Userlevels menu in N and find the level you just copied in there. If you see a list if userlevels and the map is there, congratulations! If not, then you may have moved N.exe or the userlevels.txt out of their original location. If you want them easily accessible, make shortcuts to them on your desktop instead of dragging them out of the folder.

If your problem solved? If yes, say yes, and if not... well, state the problem.

For further questions you may have, you should check out the following links:

The FAQs - Some good stuff you need to know.

The N Wiki - Tons of articles regarding N-related projects and game information.

You should also check the Forum Rules. We don't want you to end up getting a warn, or worse, a suspension.

Welcome to the Metanet Forums, and be sure to have a nice day.

Um...

On the highscores menu, the individual levels always start out at 90 seconds, unlike in normal mode explained below. The highscorers play the levels on the Highscores menu. Go check them out. Click on an episode you've unlocked and select one of the levels, and look to the right. You'll see "Play Level *level # here*". That's where the highscorers do their runs, not in normal mode.

Hello, kclark992! Your question is a really, really simple one that is easily answered in the FAQs. Have a look:

Quote: The N FAQ
Q: How do I access the N level editor / Ned?
A: At the main menu of the game, before any sounds are played, push tilde (it's ~, under Esc)

Q: Erm, my keyboard doesn't have that button
A: Oogh... well, here are some others M&R worked out. Hope you can find at least one of 'em: , | (that's not an I or small 'l'; that's a vertical slash which on most keyboards is used by pressing Backslash while holding Shift), ^, , @, and '

And, when you're done making your level using the in-game instructions, check out your editor_manual.txt and readme.txt that come with your N download for info on how to use NED and save your levels, making/playing demos, etc. The userlevels.txt also has instructions and the means for you to add userlevels to your game.

So... that's pretty much it. Before you forget though, you should really check out these links pertaining to N, Metanet, etc.

The Frequently Asked Questions Sub-Forum

The N Wiki

And, you should really read the forum rules, found here. We don't want you to end up suspended now.

So, I welcome you to the Metanet Forums, the place (some of us) call home.

#307507 6 2007-03-24T20:50:14Z Twistkill
Quote: n-Vader, March 24, 2007 04:37 pm
k thanks, ill try uploading it on photobucket then use the URL.  One other question, how do i make it so i can post a banner or whatever you call the picture that most people have at the end of their post?  Thanks
You should read up on these:

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBCode

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forum_signature#Internet_forums

Now here are the instructions for adding images to your signature:

1. Find the image you want to use and save it to your computer. Right click on the image and go to SAVE AS. Remember to save it someplace you can remember easily.
2. You now need to save the image on a website for it to work on the forum. Many of the people are using Photobucket or Imageshack. There are other sites out there you can use, but not all allow linking outside of their graphic site. Imageshack or Photobucket generate the bbcode needed to add to your signature.
3. After your image is saved on your website, copy the bbcode that is the direct link to the image.
4. Go to edit your profile.
5. Scroll down to the Edit Signature option.
6. A new window will pop up where you will be editing your signature at. This is where you add links, photos, and text.
7. Refer to the Wikipedia article for the bbcode used to add images. Plain text can be added as well, but you can format the way you want it.
8. Once you've added everything you want to your signature click on the update button located at the bottom of the editor.

(Looks like another one, guys...)

Hello, shivers21! Your question is a really, really simple one that is easily answered in the FAQs. Have a look:

Quote: The N FAQ
Q: How do I access the N level editor / Ned?
A: At the main menu of the game, before any sounds are played, push tilde (it's ~, under Esc)

Q: Erm, my keyboard doesn't have that button
A: Oogh... well, here are some others M&R worked out. Hope you can find at least one of 'em: , | (that's not an I or small 'l'; that's a vertical slash which on most keyboards is used by pressing Backslash while holding Shift), ^, , @, and '

And, when you're done making your level using the in-game instructions, check out your editor_manual.txt and readme.txt that come with your N download for info on how to use NED and save your levels, making/playing demos, etc. The userlevels.txt also has instructions and the means for you to add userlevels to your game.

So... that's pretty much it. Before you forget though, you should really check out these links pertaining to N, Metanet, etc.

The Frequently Asked Questions Sub-Forum

The N Wiki

And, you should really read the forum rules, found here. We don't want you to end up suspended now.

So, I welcome you to the Metanet Forums, the place (some of us) call home. Official languages are English and Sarcasm or Satire. (Sometimes 1337 or n00b-speak if you provide a translation.)

(Guys, I did indeed copy this from another "OMG HELP WITH NED" thread. Bite me. =D)

Go to the Compatibility tab.

Tick the tab that says "Run this program in compatibility mode for" and select Windows XP (Service Pack 2) on the drop-down list.

#316867 2 2007-04-29T21:52:38Z Twistkill
1) Select all the of the level data in Ned (From the top box) and copy it.

You will need a NUMA account. To get one, simply fire up N, click on 'configure', enter a username and password in the boxes provided, and click 'create new user'. Congratulations, you are now a member of NUMA.

2) Now, log onto NUMA using your the username and password you used. (A link to NUMA is at the top of this forum.)

3) After that's done, click the "Submit a map" option on the left-hand side.

4) Fill in the required/desired information, such as the name of the map, description, etc. Paste the data you copied into the box that says "Map Data".

5) Click submit, and you're done! Be sure to double check your map before submitting it, because you don't want any unwanted stuff. If you submit more than 2 maps in one day, they will not show up on the newest page until those 2 have been bumped off by other maps.

If you need some map-making advice, be sure to check out Jeff Killian's guide.

If you need any other N-related questions answered, check out the N Wiki, the FAQs, and usaswim's thread. You should also read up on the Forum Rules, as well as the editor_manual and readme .txt files that came packaged with your N download.

Oh yes, and welcome to our home. (Well, for some of us, at least.) We wouldn't want you to feel unwanted, now.

#323084 2 2007-05-21T15:50:43Z Twistkill
There are a few possible issues that could be causing this...

1) Are you sure you enabled unlimited local storage? Right-click anywhere in the N window, click on Settings, click on the tab with a folder on it, put that slider all the way to the right, and then close it.

2) Are you sure you put it in the right directory and you copied the right file? Don't copy any of the folder that the .sol with your progress is in, just copy the file itself and put it where the empty one is located.

3) Is practice mode enabled in the configure menu? If it is, then you should disable it.

Try these possible solutions, beat one episode, close N, reopen N, and see if your progress was saved. If none of these work, then your .sol file is either corrupted, or you gave it too many grilled cheese sandwiches.

While we're still on the topic of the age limit of M-rated games, I personally think that the ESRB doesn't realize how desensitized the younger kids have become to violence and sex as it is.

Oh, lemme share one of my best moments of God of War 2 I've had so far:

I got over a 2,600 hit combo on the final battle with Zeus on God Mode with the combined effort of the Urn of Prometheus (Granting me infinite Rage of the Titans) and simply holding down the square button while it was active. You must have Level 5 Athena's Blades to perform it. See, holding down the square button during Rage of the Titans actually deals little damage, but it hits very rapidly in a wide arc, so you can rack up an insanely large combo on really tough enemies like Cyclops or the bosses like Euryale or Perseus.

In addition, when you try to constantly attack while Kratos is in his normal state, if he gets hit, then he stumbles and stops his attacks. However, Rage of the Titans actually reduces the damage of all hits and you do not stumble if you're hit while it is active. Some htis are even completely negated. Plus, during the entirety of the time it is enabled, the time limit you have between your attacks to continue a combo doesn't end until you deactivate it.

The way I see this...

All genres of music are made to create a certain mood or atmosphere - there are exceptions, of course, but this is the general concept of it. We have come to know Classical as soothing or otherwise relaxing, Rock is more energetic or "alive", etc. but there are those aforementioned exceptions. Our moods should determine what genre (Or, if you're like Keron, your style of only one particular genre) of music we want to listen to at any particular point in time. I know that if I'm feeling upset or angry, I will put on Three Day's Grace, Staind, Disturbed, etc. If I'm feeling light-hearted... okay, I don't have any "light" music on my computer, but you're getting the point here?

We don't have to be confined to one genre due to our subjectivity or bias, and we shouldn't, due to the fact that specific genres, are, for the most part, used to create a certain feeling or atmosphere we want.

#331745 5 2007-06-16T04:53:23Z Twistkill
Guys, he said he doesn't have practice mode on.

The gold you collect does add to your remaining time for the episode, but if you still don't beat each level in the episode in a fixed and invisible 90 second limit, then it isn't recorded as a personal best. So, you could take more than 90 seconds to beat a level but still have time left on the clock, because they're seperate.

I hope I explained that well enough...

ksg: Go to the Highscores menu and select the first episode in the first column, which would be 00-0. Look in the upper-left hand corner of the screen and you'll see the personal bests for each level in the episode. If you have a time recored for each level there, then select the next episode, check if there are personal bests, and rinse and repeat until you come across levels that do not have recorded times. You must redo the episodes that have missing times, and the levels that do not have personal bests within those episodes must be completed within 90 seconds individually; Not what's counting down at the top of your screen.

I hope your problem is fixed.

The editor_manual.txt, which is attached in the case that you don't have it, has the relatively simple instructions for this, as well as the other features of Ned:

Quote
---Playing Back a Recorded Demo ---

Note!!  Always paste demo data into the lower text box!

The top textbox should be filled with level data corresponding to the demo -- the level in which the demo should be played.

1. Press [L] to pull up the textboxes.  Paste level data into the upper text box, paste demo data into the lower text box.

2. Press [L] to load your level.

3. Press [3] to load your demo.

4. Press [Q] to initiate playback of the demo.

5. Press [P] to start viewing the demo.

6. Make sure caps lock is on!

Follow those steps and you should be viewing demos in no time.
