Ohh, a common problem that is bothering you.

You start with 152 userlevels, and you can add more, which is what you are trying to accomplish. However, you have this issue. See, the original copies of your userlevels.txt and your main N.exe must be in the same place for them to be in sync and work properly. You must have physically moved either one of them somewhere else, yes? Whether they are in a folder, on your desktop, or anywhere on your computer, they must be in the same place. So, place those 2 things in any folder together, and make shortcuts to them on your desktop to gain easy accessibility.

Oh, and I have some other places you should check out before asking further questions...

The N Wiki

FAQs

Also, the Forum Rules are of utmost importance. We wouldn't want you to end up suspended, but you seem content on adhering to the rules so far.

Have fun.

The code for this is

[spoiler*=the text to be spoilerified]What it contains[/*spoiler]

And for images:

[spoiler*=[img]image link here[/img]]stuff to be shown[/*spoiler]

(Take out the stars)

You can basically put large or otherwise distracting things in your signature between the spoiler tags so it will be hidden, but it will still have to load. Also, your entire signature, even with all spoilers expanded, which includes images, text/quotes, etc. cannot be wider than 600 pixels and longer than 335 pixels.

#357872 14 2007-08-21T13:56:24Z Twistkill
Quote: Viridovix, August 21, 2007 08:18 am
Um... I'm just naturally depressed, really. I have no reason to be, but someone called it "Clinical Depression"?
Mm, I believe that's incorrect... a "natural" depression is an everyday one, or something that just makes you feel sad for a while, which happens to pretty much everyone. Clinical Depression is more severe, it is something that I have:

"clinical depression is a serious, potentially lethal systemic disorder characterized by the psychiatric profession as interlocking physical, affective, and cognitive symptoms that have consequences for function and survival well beyond sad or painful feelings.

... to have five of these symptoms over a two-week period. These include:

* Feelings of overwhelming sadness and/or fear, or the seeming inability to feel emotion (emptiness).
* A decrease in the amount of interest or pleasure in all, or almost all, daily activities.
* Changing appetite and marked weight gain or loss.
* Disturbed sleep patterns, such as insomnia, loss of REM sleep, or excessive sleep (hypersomnia).
* Psychomotor agitation or retardation nearly every day.
* Fatigue, mental or physical, also loss of energy.
* Intense feelings of guilt, nervousness, helplessness, hopelessness, worthlessness, isolation/loneliness and/or anxiety.
* Trouble concentrating, keeping focus or making decisions or a generalized slowing and obtunding of cognition, including memory.
* Recurrent thoughts of death (not just fear of dying), desire to just "lie down and die" or "stop breathing", recurrent suicidal ideation without a specific plan, or a suicide attempt or a specific plan for committing suicide.
* Feeling and/or fear of being abandoned by those close to one."

I have all of those symptoms except for the thoughts regarding suicide and the changes in appetite/weight loss. Suicide is idiotic.

The Simple Action Competition!

Welcome everyone. As you may already have guessed, this will be a map-making competition based only on how simple you can make an action map while making it as fun as possible. It sounds rather easy, doesn't it? Well, get to it, then!
Rules and Guidelines:

The maps must be in the action category. No races, DDAs, or puzzles... just the type that started it all.
You must create your maps from scratch. You are not allowed to use any old maps on NUMA.
The map must not contain more than 35 tiles, 25 objects (includes gold), and 10 enemies. The ninja and exits do not count as objects.
You will submit the map to NUMA, and provide a link to this thread in the description. Also, please post the NUMA link here as well.
You have up to 4 submissions, but only your best one counts.

There will be 3 judges and 20 competitors. You may ask to be a judge, so this is first come, first serve. However, if you are a judge, then you cannot take part in the competition itself. If more people wish to compete, I may consider adding you to the roster. I am participating in this competition myself, so I am one of the competitors.

The deadline to submit maps is October 17th.
Grading System

/5 Points for how well the map flows. Is there a path to follow that provides high-speed routes, or is it cumbersome to move around on the map?
/15 Points for how fun the map is. Does it make you want to play it again?
/10 Points for difficulty/enemy placement. Is the map overbearingly difficult or is it too easy?

The grades will be added together, thus the total will be out of 90. Whoever has the highest score wins!

deadly_cookie, in case you haven't noticed: At the top of this forum, there is a large notice that specifically states that any ideas that add warfare, multiplayer, or extra keys are not going to be implemented whatsoever. N is a simplistic game in which the main objective is to simply avoid enemies, collect enough gold to sustain your life, and exit the area via an exit door. Your ideas are much too complicated for a game like N.

Jetpacks - Pretty much cheating half of the levels, and also adds another key to be used.

Duck/crawl - You would obviously move slower, and this would not protect your from floorguards. It really doesn't seem plausible to add in the game.

Rope climbing/swinging - While this will never make it into N, Metanet's upcoming shareware game Robotology is going to revolve around some type of physics system using ropes.

Grenades - This is considered warfare/fighting/competition of some kind.

Kick/punch - Same as above.

Multiplayer - N+ is coming out on the PSP, DS, and Xbox Live Arcade (XBLA) hopefully by the end of this year. It will feature multiplayer maps, so be sure to look out for it!

Teleport platforms - Well, teleporting can already be accomplished via a tutorial that LV has set up... located here.

Particle based water - I do not have any feedback on this, sorry.

Oh, and for future reference, please take a look at some of these:

The FAQs (Which can now be updated by certain members of the community, so check back on them once in a while.)
The N Wiki - A plethora of information and details about several things regarding N and the community are located here.

In addition, you should read up on the Forum Rules... we wouldn't want you to end up suspended for something silly.

So... welcome to the forum, deadly cookie. Glad you could join us.

I believe anorexia results from how a woman views her body. She decides that she is "fat" when she really is not, and then goes on hefty diets, as well as vomiting, to lose more and more mass until she is at an unhealthy body weight. Some of the symptoms of anorexia may include extra hair growth (the body is making up for its lack of extra weight to stay warm), stained or decayed teeth (from the vomiting/acid), and, obviously, a sudden weight loss when the person is already at a healthy weight.

Like Dave said, this could be from our society's view of what women should look like, and then this causes cognitive problems that start the anorexia process. However, I do believe that there could be other factors influencing the outcome.

I'm only using women as an example here - obviously men can suffer from it too, but it's more "known", so to speak, for women. I'm not attempting to be sexist in any way... nor am I, at any rate.

#380922 2 2007-11-19T20:17:35Z Twistkill
Ah yes, the dreaded sticky keys dilemma... I have 2 solutions for you:

1) If you want to simply change the jump key to something else, then you can change all of the keys to anything you wish in the Configure menu of N, on the upper right hand side. This is obviously a simple solution.

2) If you still want to keep shift as your jump key,then you can deactivate the Stickykeys shortcut on Windows XP. This will take a little more time, but it will also get rid of it for any other programs that require the usage of the shift key, such as Microsoft Word. Go to Control Panel -> Accessibility Options. In the Keyboard tab, make sure that the "Use Stickykeys" box is unticked. In addition, you should also click on the Settings button and untick the box that says "Use shortcut" option. This will completely stop the "pressing shift 5 times" problem that you're experiencing.

Good luck with N.

#399423 9 2008-01-10T15:57:16Z Twistkill
Wedgie: What levels are your characters at? In one of my save games I'm a Guardian at level 30, with Veradux and Gligus as my partners. I have another Guardian saveslot around level 21 or so, a Destroyer save slot in the high 10s, and an Assasin save slot in the low 20s. Gunslinger sucks, I don't use it.

Replay the Paladin battle over and over again to get all of his clothing, and put all of it on Veradux. The stats are all excellent for his character and the poison piercing is at 600 for each piece. When Veradux does a poison attack, it will do a huge amount of damage... the subsequent damage for the 4 turns is only based on his strength, however.

The Judgement rifle is the best weapon in the game, especially Guardians, for every character except for Destroyers and Gunslingers. 50 magic, 30 strength, 30 vitality, 25 lightning piercing and 25 physical piercing.

The diadvantage of starting with your character as an Assassin is that you cannot use Shadow Blend; it's an NPC only move, like Amber... it increases speed by 500% for 4 turns, which ridiculously increases the Assassin's piercing damage. Amber can do like 1200 damage in one move at level 15 when this is enabled.

Here's a guide for the partners you should use when you unlock all of the characters:

If you start as the Guardian class, in my opinion the easiest class to use because their only weakness is a little bit of speed, so upgrade that above everything else: Veradux and Amber/Amber and Gligus/Veradux and Gligus

if you start as the Destroyer class, very high strength and good vitality, but somewhat slow, and pretty much zip in the way of magic: Veradux and Amber/Amber and Teco/Veradux and Teco

Is you start as the Assassin class... difficult to stay alive but with such a high speed rating, and the armor in the fourth area drastically increasing it, you can dodge hits more often than the other classes, and have lots more piercing damage, especially if you upgrade Smash and Master Strike: Veradux and Gligus/Veradux and Teco/Teco and Gligus

Don't even bother with the Gunslinger class. Although the magic moves have lots of special effects and can be deadly, you have low vitality and will be slaughtered in only a few hits unless you upgrade Intervention and Heroic Motivation...

Tip: The electro bolt is an absolutely essential move for Guardians. The armor they get throughout the game, especially in the last area, all has high lightning piercing ratings... combine this with Sunder, Wound, and the Magic Bolt attack, as well as the amount of damage being directly correlated to your strength and magic rating, you can do a ridiculous amount of damage and it will debuff enemies accoridng to its level ie. level 1 Electro Bolt will remove 1 buff, level 2 will remove 2, etc.

The same applies to Heroic Motivation - health recovered is 170% of your strength and magic at level 1 plus it removes one negative effect, 230% for level 2 and removes 2 neg. effects, 290% at level and removes 3 negative effects.

Anyone else got some strategies or tips for everyone?

The all too well-known arguments of suffering in the world, empirical evidence (acting under the false pretense that it's the only thing that confirms something is real), and the illogical nature (once again assuming that if something is illogical then we shouldn't take heed of what it says or does) of omnipotence is used often in religious debates regarding God.

Forgive the preachiness, just hear me out:

Aren't any of you glad that you actually have a choice in the matter? When He created us, He wanted us to choose to obey Him rather than forcing us. Wouldn't you rather have your child obey you out of love and respect rather than forcefully adhering them (via anterior motives or otherwise) to your whim? There wouldn't be any satisfaction in forcing us to obey him because then we wouldn't have any diversity on Earth anymore, not to mention He would be essentially controlling what we do. Everyone would be going to Heaven and all things would be completely identical in all aspects of life. We would all be robots, essentially. What would be the point of living in a finite body here on Earth, where everything is identical, rather than just staying in Heaven?

Science arrives at conclusions using empirical evidence. People mistakenly believe that it must be the only thing that proves something is real and anything that says otherwise is wrong and not provable. Faith, at least in a church environment, causes many spiritual things to happen. People speak in tongues, get goosebumps when they're worshiping, fall over in the spirit, among other things. Who is anyone to claim these things are all fictional? You were not that person and you were not experiencing those things. In order to make any sort of claim against it, you must experience it yourself. You can't observe the phenomenas of God with "evidence" and "theories".

I've always wanted to hold a moderator position on a large (and amazing) forum such as this one, because it feels like I'd make more of a difference than being a moderator on a dinky general forum made by Joe Shmoe.

- I've been here since February of 2006, and despite some ups and downs, I've always felt like I've been appreciated here. The people here always reassured me of how awesome I am, and even if I didn't believe it sometimes, I see why they were saying that. I've also been a Metanember for quite some time now and have a large enough post count to show that I've seen plenty of good and bad times on this forum. This makes me a good candidate for the moderator position because of the general consensus that I'm a positive attribute of the Metanet forums.

- I have a good understanding of how forum mechanics work from several past moderation jobs (albeit they were not very big forums and I usually knew the person anyway), and even if I'll be required to learn new things or consider different approaches to handle a situation, I consider myself a fast learner.

- Seeing as school isn't as frustrating as it was last year, I have plenty of free time to spend here. I'm usually available after 3:30 PM on weekdays until 11:30 at night, EST, except Friday nights, because I go to my youth group at church downtown. Also, when February rolls around, seeing as I only need to finish one semester of high school, I'll have all the free time in the world, with the exception being finding employment.

- I've always considered this forum special, both for its excellent community and effort we put in for this little flash game. We've done many different things, including many interviews/contests with Mare and Raigan, we have an IRC channel that is quite active, we have literally hundreds of thousands of maps available, including numerous map packs made by members here. There's also special projects like the Metanet Orchestra, the Forum Image Worm, and Metasecret, and many more. Then there's the hilarious forum pranks that sporadically appear to keep this place exciting, with the most recent one being the hostile Tetris takeover. It's a shame that I missed out on that!

The point of that paragraph was to say that I want to be involved. I want to be a contributor, be a part of, or do something to help out with these special projects and pranks. I feel as if a moderator position will greatly assist me in having my services requested and leave a good impression among any newer members that will (hopefully) revere me and what I do.

- I was warned only once, and it was a joke to begin with. There was a GLAYSHUR fad that spread across the forum like a disease a while back, and after I posted that word, Suki warned me just because he pledged to purge it out of the forums by banning everyone who posted it on that day. Hilarious, but obviously not a warn for violation of any forum rules.

I sincerely hope you consider me as one of the Metanet staff members based on these factors. I consider the moderator position here something not to be taken lightly or for granted.
